en: Section B Interview.
zh: B节：访谈。

en: In this section you will hear one interview.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段访谈。

en: The interview will be divided into two parts.
zh: 这段访谈分为两部分。

en: At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said.
zh: 每部分结束后，将就刚才所说的内容提出五个问题。

en: Both the interview and the questions will be spoken once only.
zh: 访谈和问题都只读一遍。

en: After each question, there will be a ten-second pause.
zh: 每个问题之后会有十秒钟的停顿。

en: During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C, and D, and mark the best answer to each question on Answer Sheet two.
zh: 请利用停顿时间阅读A、B、C、D四个选项，并在答题卡二上标出每题的最佳答案。

en: You have thirty seconds to preview the questions.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览题目。

en: Now listen to part one of the interview.
zh: 现在请听访谈的第一部分。

en: Questions 1 to 5 are based on part 1 of the interview.
zh: 第1至5题根据访谈的第一部分提问。

en: Good morning, Dr. Harley.
zh: 早上好，哈利博士。

en: Thank you very much for coming on our radio talk.
zh: 非常感谢您来到我们的广播访谈节目。

en: We know that you are an applied linguist specializing in second language acquisition.
zh: 我们知道，您是一位专门研究第二语言习得的应用语言学家。

en: Right.
zh: 是的。

en: So, today, urmm... we’ll look at this issue.
zh: 那么，今天，嗯……我们就来探讨这个问题。

en: Now, first, Dr. Harley, could you please tell us what is second language acquisition?
zh: 首先，哈利博士，能否请您告诉我们，什么是第二语言习得？

en: Well, second language acquisition is “happens when a child or adult has already become competent at a language, and then, urmm... they attempt to learn another.”
zh: 嗯，第二语言习得是指这样的情况：儿童或成年人已经掌握了一种语言，然后，嗯……再尝试学习另一种语言。

en: OK, most people think, including me, it is difficult to learn another language.
zh: 好的。大多数人，包括我自己，都觉得学习另一种语言很难。

en: What are the reasons? Why is it so?
zh: 原因有哪些？为什么会这样？

en: Well, there are a number of reasons for this.
zh: 嗯，这有好几个原因。

en: Urmm... first, there have been research studies.
zh: 嗯……首先，已经有一些相关研究。

en: They have shown that some aspects of language learning, especially syntax, are more difficult beyond a certain age, say after around 12 years of age.
zh: 研究表明，语言学习的某些方面，尤其是句法，在超过一定年龄后，例如大约十二岁以后，会变得更难。

en: So, age plays an important role in language learning?
zh: 所以，年龄在语言学习中起着重要作用，是吗？

en: Yes. But that’s not the only reason.
zh: 是的。但这并不是唯一的原因。

en: Oh, is that so?
zh: 哦，是这样吗？

en: Yes. For example, umm, time and interest.
zh: 是的。例如，嗯，时间和兴趣。

en: Old children and adults often have less time and motivation to learn a second language.
zh: 年龄较大的孩子和成年人，往往没有那么多时间和动力去学习第二语言。

en: Another is related to the similarities and differences between one’s mother tongue and a second language.
zh: 另一个原因与母语和第二语言之间的相似性及差异有关。

en: We find that learners will experience difficulty when their mother tongue and the second language they are learning differ.
zh: 我们发现，当母语与正在学习的第二语言存在差异时，学习者就会遇到困难。

en: In general, the more idiosyncratic a feature is in a particular language, relative to other languages, the more difficult it will be to acquire.
zh: 一般来说，相比其他语言，某种语言的一个特征越独特，习得这个特征就越困难。

en: Perhaps this is the key issue.
zh: 也许这正是关键所在。

en: Differences between languages cause language learning problems.
zh: 语言之间的差异会导致语言学习困难。

en: Well, this may be one of the issues here, but this cannot be the whole story, as not all differences between languages cause difficulty.
zh: 嗯，这也许是其中的一个问题，但事情并不完全如此，因为并非语言之间的所有差异都会造成困难。

en: Let me give you an example.
zh: 让我举个例子。

en: OK.
zh: 好的。

en: Research has found that many errors by Czech speakers learning English were made on syntactic constructions in which the two languages do not differ.
zh: 研究发现，母语为捷克语的人学习英语时，许多错误恰恰出现在两种语言没有差异的句法结构上。

en: Oh, really? The picture is more complicated than we’ve imagined.
zh: 哦，真的吗？情况比我们想象的还要复杂。

en: Definitely yes.
zh: 确实如此。

en: Each language learning situation is different.
zh: 每一种语言学习情境都不同。

en: So reasons vary a lot from case to case.
zh: 所以，原因会因具体情况而大不相同。

en: Now, Dr. Harley. Since learning a second language is a difficult process, you know,
zh: 那么，哈利博士，既然学习第二语言是一个艰难的过程，

en: in one way or another, are there any methods, so far, effective methods to teach a second language?
zh: 或多或少都会遇到困难，那么到目前为止，有没有什么方法，有效的方法，来教授第二语言？

en: There again. No method is absolutely effective in all situations.
zh: 这里也是一样。没有一种方法在所有情境下都绝对有效。

en: Some may prove effective, others may not.
zh: 有些方法可能有效，有些则可能无效。

en: I mean, all depending on specific conditions.
zh: 我的意思是，一切都取决于具体条件。

en: But generally speaking, there are a number of methods that have been used to teach a second language.
zh: 不过，一般来说，已经有若干种方法被用于第二语言教学。

en: Could you mention a few?
zh: 您能举出几种吗？

en: For instance, there is the traditional method.
zh: 例如，有传统教学法。

en: This method is based on translation from one language to another and it emphasizes grammar teaching.
zh: 这种方法以两种语言之间的翻译为基础，并强调语法教学。

en: Mm...
And then you have direct methods, which focuses on conversational skills and all teaching must be carried out in the second language.
zh: 然后还有直接教学法，它着重培养会话技能，而且全部教学都必须使用第二语言进行。

en: Oh, I see. Any other methods?
zh: 哦，我明白了。还有其他方法吗？

en: Yes. For example, the audiolingual method.
zh: 有的。例如，听说法。

en: This method emphasizes speaking and listening before reading and writing.
zh: 这种方法强调先进行说和听的训练，再进行读写训练。

en: How interesting!
zh: 真有意思！

en: Then you have the immersion method.
zh: 然后还有沉浸式教学法。

en: This method teaches learners exclusively through the medium of the second language.
zh: 这种方法完全以第二语言为媒介来教授学习者。

en: How?
zh: 怎么进行呢？

en: Well, it simply means that you cannot speak mother tongue.
zh: 嗯，简单来说，就是不能说母语。

en: Everything must be done in the language you are learning.
zh: 所有事情都必须用你正在学习的语言来完成。

en: To me, the most natural method of learning a new language is what I call submersion.
zh: 在我看来，学习一门新语言最自然的方式，是我所说的“完全置身其中”。

en: That is, to go to that country and be surrounded exclusively by speakers of that language.
zh: 也就是说，去到那个国家，周围接触到的全是说那种语言的人。

en: This is the end of part one of the interview.
zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。
